sources: Royal Ontario Museum, 'Living Vampires' (ROM Magazine): stomach holds about two tablespoons of blood, feeding can take nearly 20 minutes and the bat can gain as much as 60 percent of its body weight; it starts urinating almost as soon as it begins drinking; heat receptor near the nose pad helps locate a vein; it hops on its feet when approaching a sleeping animal on the ground; cuts away fur and bites a 3 to 4 mm hole with razor-sharp front teeth; saliva contains draculin, which keeps blood flowing; common vampire bats feed mostly on large mammals such as pigs and cattle, occasionally humans; victims usually keep sleeping; successful bats share blood with less successful colony members by regurgitating, and the generosity is repaid; can't survive more than a few days without a blood meal; https://www.rom.on.ca/magazine/living-vampires

Cornell Chronicle, 'Unlike other bats, vampire bats keep out of trouble by running' (Riskin and Hermanson, Nature 2005): of roughly 1,100 bat species the common vampire bat is the only one so far to break into a run on a treadmill test; runs up to about 2.5 mph; powers its run with its forelimbs (wings); native to Central and South America; feeds on cattle while they sleep, about a tablespoon of blood over about 10 minutes; https://news.cornell.edu/node/282646

Gracheva E.O. et al. (2011) 'Ganglion-specific splicing of TRPV1 underlies infrared sensation in vampire bats', Nature 476:88-91: vampire bats detect infrared heat with a TRPV1 variant in the nose pit organs, used to find hot spots for feeding; https://doi.org/10.1038/nature10245

Wilkinson G.S. (1984) 'Reciprocal food sharing in the vampire bat', Nature 308:181-184: common vampire bats regurgitate blood to roostmates, both kin and non-kin, and the sharing is reciprocal; https://doi.org/10.1038/308181a0

title: This Bat Drinks So Much Blood It Pees While It Eats 🦇

beats.say: This bat drinks so much blood, it has to pee while it's still eating.
So I shrank myself to bat size, and followed one out for dinner.
The common vampire bat, from Central and South America.
At night, it finds a sleeping cow, or a pig.
It lands nearby, and hops over on the ground.
A heat sensor on its nose finds a warm vein.
It shaves off a little fur, then razor-sharp front teeth cut a tiny hole.
Its spit has a chemical called draculin, that keeps the blood flowing.
In one meal, it can gain up to sixty percent of its body weight.
That's too heavy to fly. So it starts peeing almost as soon as it starts drinking.
Of over a thousand kinds of bats, it's the only one seen running on a treadmill.
It runs on its folded wings, like front legs.
Back in the cave, things get gross. Without blood every few days, it starves.
So when a roostmate comes home hungry, a full bat throws up blood, right into its mouth.
And the bats that share are the ones that get fed back later.
Sometimes, it even bites people. Would you sleep with your feet outside the blanket?
It runs on its hands, pees while it eats, and pays its friends in vomit.
